reading.body:
EdgeCore Ashburn AS01 publishes 114 MW of IT capacity across 685,000 square feet in Sterling, Virginia, representing roughly 2,850 racks at standard AI training density, though actual tenant configuration and workload mix remain undisclosed.

This facility ranks third by published capacity among Virginia's 25 data centers with disclosed megawatt figures, accounting for 7.1 percent of the state's 1,603 MW in published IT load. Virginia's 330 mapped facilities vastly outnumber those disclosing capacity, meaning most infrastructure remains opaque to public assessment. LEED certification confirms energy efficiency standards but does not specify power source or grid connection characteristics.

For AI scaling constraints, the facility's role is impossible to evaluate without disclosure of power supply origin, grid connection point, and actual versus available megawatt allocation. Whether the 114 MW draws from existing utility capacity, new generation, Virginia's interconnected grid, or a dedicated network directly determines its impact on state-level power availability. The absence of this data means the campus cannot be weighed against Virginia's broader electrical binding constraint on AI infrastructure growth.
